claims: n-127-candidate.yaml, n-204-candidate.yaml, n-232-candidate.yaml, n-264-candidate.yaml and n-305-candidate.yaml each state a packing of n unit squares as a packing.squares:Witness/v2 document of rational corners, with the softschema envelope, a claim block of coordinate_provenance verified and method exact-algebraic, and a certificate block (exact-rational-sat, rational_digits 36, center_dilation '1') derived from the decimal pose n-NNN-decimal-pose.yaml beside it. #1001 and the root README print the sides rounded up at 12 places as 11.801753890487, 14.802646843107, 15.759531627557, 16.773807598002 and 17.945762359659, each below the record's side at 31ddae6 by 9.1249e-3, 1.7145e-3, 1.8780e-3, 9.275e-4 and 4.7041e-3, and say each exact side less the record's exact side is negative in Fraction arithmetic.

The README and #1001 say each packing is a public Kaggle packing by Tomas Kodaj (tomkodaj), from his notebook 'Squares in Squares | [22.1636]' (last run 2026-11-13 09:48 UTC, downloaded 10:17 UTC that day), at sides 11.801765635430, 14.802646907234, 15.759531732104, 16.773891500852 and 17.946298110350, improved further by JoeGun by 1.174e-5, 6.41e-8, 1.045e-7, 8.390e-5 and 5.358e-4: a fault-line DP of their own at 127, 204 and 232 (2026-11-13 10:42 UTC), a 600 s quench with Evan Daniel's code (evand/square-packing at 6067db5, MIT) at 264 (2026-11-14 09:42 UTC), and two quench runs then the fault-line DP at 305 (2026-11-13 13:41 and 23:40 UTC). The fault-line DP cuts pieces out of other packings along lines no square crosses and joins them by a dynamic programme; the donors are their own and public Kaggle packings, and which donors the winning pieces came from was not recorded. They did not trace what Kodaj's packings build on. They suggest credit to Kodaj as finder at all five counts, improved by JoeGun, and say credit to Kodaj alone is fair at 204 and 232, where their part is below 2e-7.

The README says the exact coordinates come from this repository's packing-witness promote --strategy robust-rational --max-side-increase 1e-11 at 31ddae6, after every f64 centre was pushed away from the centroid by a factor of at least 1 + 1e-12, and that packing-witness verify (packing-witness-verify.txt) reports VERIFIED, exact-algebraic, for all five, testing 8,001, 20,706, 26,796, 34,716 and 46,360 pairs, so that it does not check the rounding independently; and that check.py, written apart from this repository's code in Fraction arithmetic with no tolerance and no distance filter (check-output.txt), reports VALID for all five and refused three broken copies of the n = 127 witness. They make no optimality, rigidity or KKT claim, did not measure the least pair margin or the contraction margin, and say AI agents wrote and ran the search code, the checker and the filing, under JoeGun's direction. The issue also quotes the Kaggle per-puzzle leaderboard's side-only entries below the claims at all five counts, and Kodaj's n = 270 at 16.927469594094, which it does not claim. Those statements are the author's; no source program ran here.
